case_study_packaging.readiness_notes: All key elements are present: named healthcare client, clear procurement challenges, $780K quantified savings across eight categories, multiple documented proof points.
case_study_packaging.headline: Women’s health platform captures $780K annual savings in 5 months, delivering 3.5× ROI through strategic sourcing
case_study_packaging.client_problem_statement: Advantia Health, a rapidly expanding women’s health provider operating 60+ clinics, managed purchasing through disparate systems inherited from acquisitions and lacked a centralized procurement function. Fragmented vendor relationships, inconsistent pricing, and incomplete spend visibility put pressure on margins and jeopardized private-equity value-creation objectives. Leadership needed a partner that could quickly unlock savings and embed disciplined purchasing processes across ten high-spend categories.
case_study_packaging.client_problem_anonymized: A rapidly expanding women’s health platform operating 60+ clinics managed purchasing through disparate systems inherited from acquisitions and lacked a centralized procurement function. Fragmented vendor relationships, inconsistent pricing, and incomplete spend visibility put pressure on margins and jeopardized objectives set by the private equity sponsor. Leadership needed a partner that could quickly unlock savings and embed disciplined purchasing processes across ten high-spend categories.
approach_summary: Analyzed $19 million in annual spend across 10 categories, validating $1.37 million in achievable savings and prioritizing quick-win opportunities.
Renegotiated the client’s Athenahealth revenue-cycle contract, cutting fees from 3.39 % to 3.15 % and securing retroactive credits worth $259K annually.
Ran competitive RFPs and vendor consolidation initiatives—moving all clinics to McKesson as prime distributor and benchmarking lab and IT managed-service pricing.
Designed and began implementing an in-house sonography staffing model, replacing outsourced scans and targeting 19 % cost reduction without disrupting clinical coverage.
Implemented demand-management policies such as a 5-unit IUD order minimum and enrolled practices in Bayer’s replacement program, capturing otherwise lost value.
case_study_packaging.value_delivered_blurb: Treya delivered $780K in verified annual run-rate savings—73 % above the contractual guarantee and equal to 3.5× the project’s fixed fee. Nearly $500K was fully implemented within the 5-month engagement, with the balance in final contracting. Beyond hard dollars, Treya standardized IUD purchasing, extended payment terms to 60 days, and stood up an in-house sonography recruiting capability to sustain savings long term.
where_we_were_unique: Realized first savings in just 45 days through targeted policy changes and rapid contract renegotiation.
Leveraged deep healthcare procurement expertise to secure best-in-class terms with Athenahealth, McKesson, LabCorp, and specialty device manufacturers under significant switching constraints.
Hands-on change management enabled a seamless shift to an in-house sonography model while maintaining service levels across 60+ clinics.
Exceeded the 2× savings guarantee by 73 %, providing a 3.5× return on Treya’s fees.
